newsitem.title: USA: Glickman reiterates interest in grain reserve.
newsitem.headline: Glickman reiterates interest in grain reserve.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman reiterated his interest Tuesday in authorizing a farmer-owned grain reserve to help farmers minimize risk.

In an interview, Glickman said USDA is considering supporting some minor changes in the farm bill, focusing on ways to provide a better safety net for farmers. He said that a grain reserve would be an option to help farmers.

"I've wanted to look at the issue of a farmer-owned grain reserve, and/or variations of it, that would give farmers more ability in the marketing of their crop, without making any radical changes in the 1996 farm bill because those would unlikely be passed by Congress," Glickman said in an interview.
Glickman said that the USDA would recommend some technical changes in the farm bill, especially in the areas of farmer credit and landlord/tenant relationship issues.
"I do think there will be a technical corrections effort" by Congress, said Glickman. "There's no doubt there will need to be one."
